## Your logs no longer pile up forever

WGSmart keeps a log of what the daemon does, and until now it was bounded only by size — 8 MB,
then the oldest half was dropped. That sounds tidy and is not: a quiet machine keeps **months**
inside 8 MB, while one flapping tunnel fills the same 8 MB in **minutes**. Same setting, retention
anywhere from an hour to a year depending on your network.

That matters more here than in most apps, because the log records which tunnels were up, when, and
which names got resolved. On a VPN client that is a record of where you have been.

**Settings ▸ Daemon now has "Keep logs for": 24 hours · 7 days · 30 days · Until full.** The
daemon enforces it on a timer — it holds while the app is closed, and it survives a restart. The
size cap still runs alongside it; whichever limit is reached first is the one that cuts.

There is also a **Clear now** button, for when you want the log gone this second rather than on a
schedule.

> **Heads up: the default is 30 days, and it applies on first run.** If your daemon has been
> logging since 1.0.0, entries older than 30 days will be dropped shortly after you update.
> Choose **Until full** first if you want to keep them.

---

## Fixed

**The diagnostics panel was telling you the wrong places to look.** Settings showed a socket at
`/tmp/wgsmart.sock` — which does not exist; the real one is under `/var/run` — and a "Config Dir"
of `wg_ondemand_4mac/wg_conf/`, a leftover from the shell-script project WGSmart replaced, that no
code has read in a very long time. Both were hard-coded strings that had quietly drifted from
reality. They are now reported by the daemon itself, so they cannot drift again, and a path the
daemon has not reported shows as unknown instead of as a confident guess.

**The "Domains" tab wrapped onto two lines** in Traffic Rules, breaking the row. The four tabs
split the width evenly, which left "IP" holding 35pt it did not need while "Domains" came up 1.3pt
short. The labels are slightly smaller now and fit with room to spare.

**Long names are readable again.** Tunnel names, endpoints, domains, app rules, port rules and
CIDRs get cut off when they do not fit — unavoidable, since the length is yours, not ours — but
hovering now shows the full value.

## Fixed on Linux

**The generated web-UI password was occasionally 24–27 characters instead of 28.** Never a weak
one, but the documentation said 28 and was wrong about 0.3% of the time. It is now exactly 28.

**Extracting the hub tarball printed 14 warnings** about `LIBARCHIVE.xattr.com.apple.provenance` —
harmless macOS metadata, but a wall of warnings is a poor first impression of a download. Gone.

**The web UI warned that `/etc/wgsmart/webui.hash` was mode 0640 and should be 0600** — while 0640
is exactly what the installer creates, and is the *stricter* arrangement: the service can read the
file but not rewrite it. A warning that fires on the recommended configuration teaches people to
ignore warnings, so it now checks who the group actually is.

---

## Still true

- **Not notarized.** macOS warns on first launch, and the warning is accurate: this build is
  ad-hoc signed, not Developer ID signed. Right-click ▸ Open, or clear the quarantine attribute.
- **App routing on macOS is per-UID**, not per-process — it routes everything a given user runs.
  That is the honest description of what the mechanism does.
- **The Linux hub's packaging is verified; its VPN is not.** Installing, upgrading and the browser
  UI were tested end to end on a real systemd system. No tunnel has carried traffic on real
  hardware — every `nft`, `ip` and cgroup call is covered only by unit tests.
- Windows is not supported.

## Verifying this download

```sh
shasum -a 256 -c WGSmart-1.0.4.pkg.sha256
```

The `.sig` files are Ed25519 signatures over the same artifacts. The app checks them
automatically on every update, and since 1.0.3 it checks the update manifest's signature too.
